newsitem.title: USA: Malcolm X widow has skin grafts for burns.
newsitem.headline: Malcolm X widow has skin grafts for burns.

text.p: The widow of Malcolm X, badly burned in a fire allegedly set by her troubled grandson, had seven hours of skin graft surgery on Wednesday, hospital officials said.
"She withstood the procedure considerably well but she still remains in critical but stable condition," a spokeswoman at the Jacobi Hospital Burn Unit in the Bronx borough of New York City said.
Betty Shabazz, 63, suffered third-degree burns over 80 percent of her body in a fire on Sunday. A third-degree burn is one that extends deep into the skin's underlying tissue.
A team of six doctors removed about 20 percent of her dead skin in the operation, which began at 11:22 a.m. EDT (1522 GMT) and lasted until 6:30 p.m. EDT (2230 GMT).
"It's not unusual for skin grafting to take this long. It's a complicated procedure," Nina Johnson, a hospital spokeswoman, said. Shabazz will have more skin grafts on Thursday afternoon.
The operation was led by Dr. Bruce Greenstein, director of the burn unit. Greenstein also took a sample of Shabazz's skin to be cultured and grown in a laboratory for grafting later.

Shabazz's 12-year-old grandson, Malcolm Shabazz, named after his controversial grandfather, is accused of setting the fire at her Yonkers, New York, apartment. A judge on Tuesday ordered him to have medical and psychological tests before returning to Westchester Family Court on Friday.
Law enforcement officials alleged Malcolm splashed fuel at the front door of Shabazz's apartment and set it ablaze. He had been staying there for the last three weeks.

Bill Tatum, a family friend, described Malcolm "as a disturbed child of trauma." He said the boy was angry with his grandmother and wanted her to send him back to his mother, Qubilah Bahiyah Shabazz, 36, in Texas.

Qubilah Shabazz, a daughter of civil rights leader Malcolm X and Betty Shabazz, saw her father assassinated at Harlem's Audubon Ballroom in 1965. She was indicted in 1995 on charges she tried to hire a man to kill Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, whom her mother had accused of playing a role in Malcolm X's assassination.
Federal prosecutors dismissed the case last month.
